DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE: , The patient, a 73-year-old male with known severe peripheral vascular disease, EF 25%, and recent NSTEMI, was taken emergently to the operating room following an episode of ventricular tachycardia and transient cardiac arrest in the catheterization lab. The pericardium was opened and noted to be tense with a moderate hemopericardium secondary to CPR. Initial inspection revealed a dilated, poorly contractile left ventricle. The PDA and RPL were heavily calcified, 1.5mm targets. The LIMA was harvested in a semi-skeletonized fashion. Saphenous vein was harvested endoscopically from the left leg. Distal anastomoses were performed in sequence. Separation from cardiopulmonary bypass required significant inotropic support including epinephrine at 0.1 mcg/kg/min, norepinephrine at 0.2 mcg/kg/min, and milrinone. An intra-aortic balloon pump was placed via the left femoral artery. Total bypass time was 188 minutes; cross-clamp time was 132 minutes. Post-bypass, diffuse coagulopathy was encountered requiring massive transfusion of 8 units PRBCs, 6 units FFP, 2 units platelets, and cryoprecipitate. Chest was closed with sternal wires over large-bore chest tubes. The patient was transferred to the CVICU in critical, open-chest condition with ongoing resuscitation.
---
DESCRIPTION: Emergency four-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting in a 73-year-old male with critical left main disease, an ejection fraction of 25%, and preoperative cardiac arrest."}]

DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE: , The patient is a 54-year-old female who presented 48 hours prior with a dense left hemiplegia and NIHSS of 22. CT perfusion demonstrated complete right MCA occlusion with a large core infarct. Despite endovascular thrombectomy achieving TICI 2b recanalization, her exam acutely deteriorated with a fixed and dilated right pupil and extensor posturing. Repeat CT showed massive edema with 8 mm midline shift and uncal herniation. The patient was taken to the OR on an emergent basis. After induction, the head was placed in a Mayfield three-pin head holder. A large reverse question-mark flap was incised, the temporalis muscle was reflected anteriorly, and a wide frontotemporoparietal craniectomy flap was elevated with a diameter exceeding 14 cm. The bone flap was wrapped in moist gauze and banked in the abdominal subcutaneous tissue. The dura was opened in a cruciate fashion. Grossly edematous, hemorrhagic brain immediately herniated through the durotomy. A dural substitute was sewn in place loosely. Hemostasis was achieved with Surgicel and bipolar cautery. An intraparenchymal ICP monitor was placed in the contralateral frontal lobe via a separate stab incision. The galea and skin were closed in a single layer with interrupted nylon due to significant brain swelling. The patient was transported back to the Neuro-ICU, ventilated, with ongoing osmotherapy and hypertonic saline infusion.

DESCRIPTION: Emergent decompressive hemicraniectomy for malignant MCA syndrome with transtentorial herniation and fixed, dilated pupil."}]

Sample Name: Perimortem Cesarean Section

PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , 1. Intrauterine pregnancy at 35 weeks and 3 days. 2. Severe placental abruption. 3. Maternal hemorrhagic shock.,POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , 1. Intrauterine pregnancy at 35 weeks and 3 days. 2. Severe placental abruption. 3. Maternal hemorrhagic shock. 4. Neonatal severe hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.,OPERATION: , 1. Emergency classical cesarean section via midline vertical abdominal and uterine incisions. 2. Supracervical hysterectomy following atony. 3. Bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy.,
DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE: , The patient is a 29-year-old G2P1001 at 35 3/7 weeks gestation, admitted for observation for preeclampsia with severe features. She experienced sudden onset of severe abdominal pain and tetanic uterine contractions. On exam, fundal height had acutely increased, vaginal bleeding was dark red and continuous, and fetal heart tones were absent by Doppler. Maternal tachycardia was 140 bpm, BP dropped to 78/40. A stat exam under general endotracheal anesthesia was performed in the L&D OR without formal time-out due to the emergency. A midline vertical abdominal incision was made from umbilicus to pubis. On entry into the peritoneal cavity, approximately 2.5 liters of blood and clot were immediately evacuated. A classical longitudinal uterine incision was made sharply. A flaccid, pale female infant without respiratory effort was delivered. The infant was handed to the waiting NICU team for full resuscitation. The placenta was manually removed, revealing a 70% retroplacental clot consistent with Couvelaire uterus. The myometrium failed to contract despite uterotonics including oxytocin, methylergonovine, carboprost, and intramuscular misoprostol. Profound uterine atony and disseminated intravascular coagulation became apparent. Decision was made for a supracervical hysterectomy to arrest hemorrhage. The uterine arteries were ligated and the cervix was transected above the level of the internal os. Both ovaries were noted to be ruptured and hemorrhagic, necessitating bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Massive transfusion protocol was activated; estimated blood loss was 6.5 liters. The patient received 14 units PRBCs, 12 FFP, 3 apheresis platelets, and 2 doses of factor VIIa. Abdomen was packed and left open with a temporary vacuum-assisted closure. The patient was transferred to the SICU intubated, on four vasopressors.
---
DESCRIPTION: Perimortem cesarean section and supracervical hysterectomy performed emergently due to severe abruption, Couvelaire uterus, and massive hemorrhage."}]

[{"role": "system", "content": "You are an LLM as part of a medical assistant system, interacting with medical practitioners to improve efficiency."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Medical Specialty: Gastroenterology
Sample Name: Screening Colonoscopy with Polypectomy

INDICATION: Average-risk colorectal cancer screening in a 55-year-old male. The patient is asymptomatic with no personal history of polyps or colorectal cancer. Family history: father had a tubular adenoma at age 60. The patient has completed a split-dose polyethylene glycol bowel preparation, with clear liquid effluent.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Mild intermittent asthma, well-controlled on albuterol as needed. No cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or bleeding diathesis.

MEDICATIONS: Albuterol inhaler prn. No anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents.

ALLERGIES: No known drug allergies.

SOCIAL HISTORY: Social alcohol use, never smoker.

PROCEDURE: Screening colonoscopy with cold snare polypectomy of a 6 mm sessile polyp in the sigmoid colon.

ANESTHESIA: Conscious sedation with intravenous midazolam 3 mg and fentanyl 75 mcg administered by anesthesiology. Supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula at 2 L/min. Continuous monitoring of heart rate, blood pressure, and oxygen saturation throughout.

DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE: After obtaining informed consent and performing a time-out, the patient was placed in the left lateral decubitus position. The colonoscope (Olympus CF-HQ190L) was gently introduced through the anus and advanced under direct visualization. The rectal vault was normal. The scope was progressed to the sigmoid colon, which was tortuous but negotiable with minimal pressure. The descending colon, splenic flexure, transverse colon, hepatic flexure, and ascending colon were all thoroughly examined, revealing normal mucosa with no evidence of inflammation, diverticula, or mass lesions. The cecum was identified by the ileocecal valve, appendiceal orifice, and terminal ileum intubation. The terminal ileum appeared normal. The scope was then slowly withdrawn, and meticulous inspection was performed. In the sigmoid colon, approximately 30 cm from the anal verge, a 6 mm sessile polyp (Paris classification Is) was identified. The polyp had a smooth surface, regular vascular pattern on narrow-band imaging (NBI), and no features suggestive of submucosal invasion. Using a cold snare, the polyp was grasped, ensnared, and resected en bloc without electrocautery. The resection site showed a clean mucosal defect with no visible residual polyp tissue. Minimal oozing was noted and stopped spontaneously. The polyp was retrieved with a Roth net and placed in a formalin specimen jar, labeled with the patient's identifiers and location. The remainder of the colon was examined during withdrawal, including the descending colon, splenic flexure, transverse colon, hepatic flexure, ascending colon, and rectum. No other polyps or lesions were seen. The withdrawal time was 12 minutes. The patient tolerated the procedure well, with stable vital signs throughout. Estimated blood loss was negligible. The patient was transferred to the recovery area in stable condition. POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: Tubular adenoma, sigmoid colon, pending histopathology. PLAN: Follow-up colonoscopy in 5-10 years depending on pathology results and updated guidelines. The patient was advised to resume a normal diet and to contact the clinic if any abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, or fever occurs.
---
DESCRIPTION: Screening colonoscopy with cold snare polypectomy of a 6 mm sessile polyp in the sigmoid colon, performed for average-risk colorectal cancer screening."}]

[{"role": "system", "content": "You are an LLM as part of a medical assistant system, interacting with medical practitioners to improve efficiency."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Medical Specialty: Cardiothoracic Surgery
Sample Name: Emergency CABG x4 – Cardiogenic Shock

PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Unstable angina, acute non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction, severe three-vessel coronary artery disease, cardiogenic shock (LVEF 25%), status post failed percutaneous intervention.
POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Same as preoperative.
OPERATION: , Emergency on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting x4: left internal mammary artery to left anterior descending artery, saphenous vein graft to first obtuse marginal branch, saphenous vein graft to posterior descending artery, saphenous vein graft to right coronary artery.
SURGEON: , J. Hartley, MD
ANESTHESIA: , General endotracheal with transesophageal echocardiography.
INDICATIONS: , The patient is a 68-year-old male with a history of hypertension, diabetes, and prior stent to the LAD, who presented with crescendo angina and evolving NSTEMI. Troponin peaked at 18.2 ng/mL. Angiography revealed in-stent restenosis of the LAD, 90% left main equivalent, 95% proximal RCA, and 80% OM1. An intra-aortic balloon pump was placed for hemodynamic support. The patient developed progressive oliguria and rising lactate despite maximal medical therapy, and was taken emergently to the operating room.
DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE: , After informed consent was obtained, the patient was transferred to the hybrid OR with the IABP at 1:1 augmentation. Standard hemodynamic monitoring, pulmonary artery catheter, and TEE probe were placed. Anesthesia was induced with etomidate, fentanyl, and rocuronium, and maintained with isoflurane. The patient was prepped and draped in the usual fashion. A median sternotomy was performed. The pericardium was opened and found to be tense; the heart was poorly contractile. The left internal mammary artery was harvested with a pedicle. Endoscopic vein harvesting was used to obtain the left greater saphenous vein. Systemic heparin was given, and cannulation was accomplished with an aortic cannula and a two-stage venous cannula. Cardiopulmonary bypass was initiated. The aorta was cross-clamped, and antegrade cold blood cardioplegia was delivered via the aortic root. The heart was arrested. Esmolol and lidocaine were added to the cardioplegia. The LIMA was anastomosed end-to-side to the LAD, which was a 1.5 mm, heavily calcified vessel. The vein grafts were then anastomosed sequentially to the OM1, PDA, and RCA. All grafts had good flow measured by transit-time flowmetry. The cross-clamp time was 108 minutes. During rewarming, the heart began to fibrillate and required defibrillation. Weaning from bypass was attempted with dopamine, dobutamine, and epinephrine, but the patient remained hypotensive with a cardiac index of 1.6 L/min/m². An additional dose of milrinone was given and the IABP was increased to 100% augmentation. After 45 minutes of additional support, the patient was successfully weaned from CPB with the chest left open and packed due to coagulopathy and myocardial edema. Protamine was given. Hemostasis was achieved with argon beam coagulation and surgical packing. Temporary epicardial pacing wires were placed. The sternum was not approximated; the chest was covered with a sterile occlusive dressing. The patient was taken to the cardiovascular ICU intubated, on multiple pressors, and with the IABP in place.
FINDINGS: , Diffuse coronary atherosclerosis with heavy calcification, poor left ventricular function, extensive myocardial edema after reperfusion.
ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS: , 2500 mL; replaced with 6 units of packed red blood cells, 4 units of fresh frozen plasma, 2 units of platelets, and 1 unit of cryoprecipitate.
COMPLICATIONS: , Intraoperative coagulopathy, profound vasoplegia, inability to close the chest.
DISPOSITION: , Transferred to the cardiovascular ICU in critical condition.
---
DESCRIPTION: Emergency CABG x4 in a patient with cardiogenic shock, severe LV dysfunction, and a post-infarction state, requiring prolonged mechanical support and open chest management."}]

[{"role": "system", "content": "You are an LLM as part of a medical assistant system, interacting with medical practitioners to improve efficiency."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Medical Specialty: Neurosurgery
Sample Name: Left Decompressive Craniectomy for Acute Subdural Hematoma

PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Acute left subdural hematoma with 15 mm midline shift, uncal herniation, Glasgow Coma Scale 6 (E1 V1 M4).
POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Same.
OPERATION: , Emergency left frontotemporoparietal decompressive craniectomy, evacuation of acute subdural hematoma, insertion of intraparenchymal intracranial pressure monitor.
SURGEON: , A. Chen, MD
ANESTHESIA: , General endotracheal with rapid sequence induction.
INDICATIONS: , The patient is a 42-year-old male unrestrained driver involved in a high-speed motor vehicle collision. He was found unresponsive at the scene, intubated, and transported. CT head demonstrated a large left acute subdural hematoma with significant mass effect, effacement of the left lateral ventricle, and uncal herniation. The right pupil was dilated and fixed. The patient was taken directly to the operating room.
DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE: , The patient was positioned supine, the head was placed in a Mayfield three-pin head holder and turned to the right. A large reverse question mark incision was marked, starting at the zygoma, curving posteriorly and superiorly, ending at the midline. The scalp was infiltrated with 1% lidocaine with epinephrine. The incision was made through the galea and the scalp flap was reflected anteriorly. The temporalis muscle was elevated and reflected. Burr holes were placed at the key point and along the planned craniotomy. A frontotemporoparietal craniotomy flap was elevated using a craniotome. The bone flap was removed and noted to be intact. The dura was tense and discolored. A cruciate durotomy was performed, and immediately a large amount of clotted subdural blood was extruded under pressure. The hematoma was evacuated using suction, irrigation, and gentle dissection. The underlying brain was edematous and showed no active bleeding. The subdural space was irrigated copiously with warm saline until clear. Hemostasis was achieved with bipolar cautery and Surgicel. Because of significant brain swelling, the dura was not closed; a dural substitute was placed. The bone flap was not replaced; it was stored in a subcutaneous abdominal pocket. An intraparenchymal ICP monitor was placed in the right frontal lobe. The scalp was closed in two layers with galea aponeurotica sutures and skin staples. A sterile dressing was applied.
FINDINGS: , Acute subdural hematoma, approximately 100 mL, causing severe brain compression and herniation. No underlying contusion or subarachnoid hemorrhage.
ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS: , 1500 mL, replaced with 3 units of packed red blood cells and 2 units of fresh frozen plasma.
COMPLICATIONS: , Intraoperative hypotension requiring norepinephrine infusion, diffuse cerebral edema.
DISPOSITION: , Transferred to the surgical intensive care unit, intubated, sedated, with ICP monitor in place.
---
DESCRIPTION: Emergency decompressive craniectomy for large acute subdural hematoma with uncal herniation and elevated intracranial pressure."}]

[{"role": "system", "content": "You are an LLM as part of a medical assistant system, interacting with medical practitioners to improve efficiency."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Medical Specialty: Surgical Oncology / Colorectal Surgery
Sample Name: Emergency Hartmann's Procedure for Perforated Sigmoid Adenocarcinoma

PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Perforated sigmoid colon cancer with feculent peritonitis, sepsis, and acute kidney injury.
POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Same, with synchronous liver metastases noted intraoperatively.
OPERATION: , Emergency exploratory laparotomy, Hartmann's procedure (sigmoid colectomy with end descending colostomy and rectal stump closure), extensive peritoneal lavage.
SURGEON: , R. Patel, MD
ANESTHESIA: , General endotracheal with invasive monitoring.
INDICATIONS: , The patient is a 75-year-old female with a three-week history of altered bowel habits, weight loss, and progressive abdominal distension. She presented with acute generalized peritonitis, fever 39.2°C, heart rate 122, and hypotension. CT abdomen revealed pneumoperitoneum, a large obstructing sigmoid mass, and free fluid. Laboratory data showed WBC 22,000, lactate 4.8 mmol/L, and creatinine 2.1 mg/dL. She was taken emergently after fluid resuscitation and initiation of vasopressors.
DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE: , After informed consent, the patient was placed supine and prepped from the nipples to the thighs. A midline laparotomy was made. Upon entry into the peritoneal cavity, foul-smelling feculent fluid and purulent material were evacuated (approximately 2000 mL). The peritoneal surfaces were inflamed and fibrin-coated. The sigmoid colon was identified and found to be massively dilated with a perforated, necrotic tumor at the rectosigmoid junction. The small bowel was matted with fibrinous adhesions, which were gently lysed. The inferior mesenteric artery was isolated and ligated, and the sigmoid colon was mobilized. The upper rectum was transected with a linear stapler below the tumor, and the staple line was oversewn. The proximal descending colon was divided, and the specimen was removed. The abdomen was irrigated with 10 liters of warm saline, and careful lavage was performed in all quadrants. An end colostomy was matured at a premarked site in the left lower quadrant. Two large-bore drains were placed in the pelvis and left paracolic gutter. The fascia was closed with interrupted figure-of-eight sutures of No. 1 PDS, and the skin was left open and packed with saline-moistened gauze. During the procedure, the patient required norepinephrine, vasopressin, and epinephrine boluses. She also received 4 units of packed red blood cells, 2 units of fresh frozen plasma, and 1 unit of platelets. The liver was palpated and found to have multiple bilobar metastases, but no resection was performed. The patient was transferred to the ICU intubated and on vasopressors.
FINDINGS: , Perforated obstructing sigmoid adenocarcinoma with fecal peritonitis; generalized peritonitis; multiple liver metastases.
ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS: , 800 mL.
COMPLICATIONS: , Intraoperative hemodynamic instability, coagulopathy, and need for open abdomen management.
DISPOSITION: , Transferred to the surgical ICU in critical condition.
---
DESCRIPTION: Emergency Hartmann's procedure for perforated sigmoid cancer with feculent peritonitis and sepsis, with synchronous liver metastases."}]

[{"role": "system", "content": "You are an LLM as part of a medical assistant system, interacting with medical practitioners to improve efficiency."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Medical Specialty: Obstetrics
Sample Name: Emergency Cesarean Section for Severe Placental Abruption

PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Severe placental abruption with fetal bradycardia and maternal hemorrhage.
POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Severe placental abruption, postpartum hemorrhage from uterine atony, Couvelaire uterus.
OPERATION: , Emergency low transverse cesarean section, manual removal of placenta, B-Lynch uterine compression suture, bilateral uterine artery ligation.
SURGEON: , L. Nguyen, MD
ANESTHESIA: , General endotracheal, emergent.
INDICATIONS: , The patient is a 32-year-old gravida 2 para 1 at 36 weeks gestation who presented with acute onset of severe abdominal pain, dark vaginal bleeding, and uterine hypertonus. Fetal heart tracing showed a prolonged deceleration to 70 bpm with minimal variability. Maternal tachycardia 130, hypotension 85/50, and a falling hematocrit. Bedside ultrasound revealed a large retroplacental hematoma. The decision was made for immediate cesarean delivery.
DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE: , The patient was rapidly transferred to the operating room, and a timeout was performed. After rapid sequence induction, the abdomen was prepped and draped. A Pfannenstiel incision was made, carried down to the fascia, and the fascia was incised. The rectus muscles were separated, and the peritoneum was entered. A low transverse uterine incision was made with a scalpel, and the uterus was entered. A large amount of dark blood and clots was immediately evacuated. A male infant was delivered breech, limp with Apgars 1 and 4, and handed to the awaiting neonatal team. The placenta was delivered manually and was found to be partially adherent with a massive retroplacental clot, approximately 1500 mL. The uterine surface showed extensive Couvelaire discoloration. The uterus was exteriorized and was markedly atonic. Despite uterine massage, oxytocin infusion, intramyometrial prostaglandin, and carboprost, the uterus remained flaccid. A B-Lynch compression suture was placed using a No. 1 chromic suture, with the needle passed through the anterior and posterior uterine walls in a lateral to medial fashion, exerting compression. Bilateral uterine artery ligation was then performed with 0 Vicryl. The uterus began to contract, and bleeding diminished. The uterine incision was closed in two layers, and the uterine atony was reassessed with acceptable tone. The abdomen was irrigated, and a Jackson-Pratt drain was placed in the subfascial space. The fascia was closed with a running No. 0 PDS suture, and the skin with subcuticular monofilament. The patient received 4 units of packed red blood cells, 2 units of fresh frozen plasma, and 1 unit of cryoprecipitate during the procedure. Total estimated blood loss was 2500 mL. The patient remained intubated and was transferred to the surgical ICU. The infant was taken to the NICU, intubated, and receiving therapeutic hypothermia.
FINDINGS: , Severe placental abruption with 80% separation, Couvelaire uterus, uterine atony.
ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS: , 2500 mL.
COMPLICATIONS: , Massive hemorrhage, uterine atony, coagulopathy.
DISPOSITION: , Mother to ICU, infant to NICU.
---
DESCRIPTION: Emergency cesarean section for severe placental abruption with massive hemorrhage, uterine atony, and Couvelaire uterus."}]

[{"role": "system", "content": "You are an LLM as part of a medical assistant system, interacting with medical practitioners to improve efficiency."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Medical Specialty: Ophthalmology
Sample Name: Emergent Repair of Ruptured Globe with Corneoscleral Laceration

PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Ruptured left globe with corneoscleral laceration, iris prolapse, traumatic cataract, and vitreous hemorrhage.
POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Same.
OPERATION: , Primary repair of ruptured globe, anterior vitrectomy, iridectomy, lensectomy, and temporary keratoprosthesis with penetrating keratoplasty.
SURGEON: , K. Thomas, MD
ANESTHESIA: , General endotracheal.
INDICATIONS: , The patient is a 28-year-old male who sustained a high-velocity blunt trauma to the left eye from a projectile during a construction accident. Visual acuity was light perception with poor projection. Examination revealed a large corneoscleral laceration extending from the 10 o'clock limbus to the equator, uveal prolapse, flat anterior chamber, and a ruptured lens capsule. CT orbit demonstrated an open globe with no intraocular foreign body. The patient was taken to the operating room emergently.
DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE: , After informed consent, the patient was positioned supine and general anesthesia was administered. The left eye was prepped with povidone-iodine and draped. A lid speculum was placed. The globe was found to be extremely soft. The conjunctiva was carefully dissected to expose the full extent of the scleral laceration. The wound was debrided of necrotic tissue. The prolapsed iris was reposited, but a portion was devitalized and was excised. The ruptured lens was removed with phacoemulsification and cortical aspiration, and the lens capsule was removed. An anterior vitrectomy was performed to clear the vitreous hemorrhage. The corneoscleral wound was then meticulously closed with interrupted 10-0 nylon sutures, achieving a watertight seal. To provide a clear optical aperture and prevent limbal stem cell deficiency, a 7.5 mm temporary keratoprosthesis was inserted. The anterior chamber was reformed with balanced salt solution. A donor cornea was trephined and sutured onto the recipient bed with a combination of 16 interrupted 10-0 nylon sutures. At the conclusion, the keratoprosthesis was removed, the anterior chamber was deep, and the globe was well formed. Subconjunctival injections of cefazolin and dexamethasone were administered. A drop of atropine 1% was instilled. The eye was patched with a shield. The procedure was completed without intraoperative complication. The patient had stable vital signs throughout. The risk of endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, and sympathetic ophthalmia remains high, and the patient will require close follow-up.
FINDINGS: , Large corneoscleral laceration with uveal and lens rupture, vitreous hemorrhage, no retinal detachment visible.
ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS: , Less than 50 mL.
COMPLICATIONS: , None immediate.
DISPOSITION: , Transferred to the post-anesthesia care unit for admission to the inpatient ophthalmology ward.
---
DESCRIPTION: Emergent repair of a ruptured left globe with extensive corneoscleral laceration, traumatic cataract, and vitreous hemorrhage, utilizing a primary penetrating keratoplasty."}]
